B1.1.1.1.1.sub_strand: 1. Why and How We Study History
B1.1.1.1.1.cs_desc: Demonstrate understanding of what history is about and how it is part of everyday life.
B1.1.1.1.1.ind_desc: Explain that history deals with past human activities.
B1.1.1.1.1.competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
B1.1.1.1.1.resources: Picture cards of past events; birthday calendar; family photo album; timeline cards; story books; radio/TV documentary clip
B1.1.1.1.1.keywords: history, past, human activities, everyday life, events, evidence
B1.1.1.1.1.assessment: Oral Q&A; timeline sequencing; past-event drawing

B1.1.1.1.2.sub_strand: 1. Why and How We Study History
B1.1.1.1.2.cs_desc: Demonstrate understanding of what history is about and how it is part of everyday life.
B1.1.1.1.2.ind_desc: Describe how sources of historical evidence help us find out about past human activities.
B1.1.1.1.2.competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration; Digital Literacy
B1.1.1.1.2.resources: Birthday register/manila card; family photographs; festival costume pictures; songs/rhymes; video of birthday/wedding/festival
B1.1.1.1.2.keywords: sources, evidence, past, birthdays, festivals, photographs, oral tradition
B1.1.1.1.2.assessment: Show-and-tell album; source-sorting task; class discussion rubric

B1.1.4.2.1.ind_desc: State the similarities and differences between the communities where learners live.
B1.1.4.2.1.competencies: Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship; Creativity & Innovation; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
B1.1.4.2.1.resources: Community walk; pictures of old chapel, post office, chief's palace; sketch books; crayons; historical site flashcards
B1.1.4.2.1.keywords: community, history, similarities, differences, historical sites, local
B1.1.4.2.1.assessment: Community site sketch & compare; oral presentation; Venn diagram

B1.2.3.1.1.cs_desc: Demonstrate understanding of why Ghana used to be called the 'Gold Coast'.
B1.2.3.1.1.ind_desc: Explain why, in the past, Ghana was known as the Gold Coast.
B1.2.3.1.1.competencies: Digital Literacy; Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
B1.2.3.1.1.resources: World map / Africa map; internet tablet; pictures of ancient Ghana Empire; gold dust sample pictures; Dr. J.B. Danquah portrait
B1.2.3.1.1.keywords: Ghana, Gold Coast, name change, ancient Ghana Empire, J.B. Danquah, costa da mina
B1.2.3.1.1.assessment: Oral explanation; map location task; matching exercise

B1.2.3.1.2.cs_desc: Demonstrate understanding of why Ghana used to be called the 'Gold Coast'.
B1.2.3.1.2.ind_desc: Recall when the name Ghana came into formal use.
B1.2.3.1.2.competencies: Creativity & Innovation; Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship; Communication & Collaboration
B1.2.3.1.2.resources: Timeline cards 1957; parliament dramatization props; Ghana flag; resource person; story cards
B1.2.3.1.2.keywords: name Ghana, formal use, 1957, independence, parliament, Gold Coast to Ghana
B1.2.3.1.2.assessment: Dramatization rubric; sequencing timeline; short oral quiz

B1.2.5.1.1.cs_desc: Show understanding of significant roles played by Ghanaians from different walks of life.
B1.2.5.1.1.ind_desc: Identify Ghanaians of diverse fields who have contributed significantly to national development.
B1.2.5.1.1.competencies: Creativity & Innovation; Digital Literacy; Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship
B1.2.5.1.1.resources: Pictures/posters: Theodosia Okoh – National flag; Amon Kotei – Coat of Arms; Baba Yara – Football; Ephraim Amu – Music; Kofi Antubam – Art; Kwaw Ansah – Film; documentary video; internet
B1.2.5.1.1.keywords: Theodosia Okoh, Amon Kotei, Baba Yara, Ephraim Amu, Kofi Antubam, Kwaw Ansah, national development, contributions
B1.2.5.1.1.assessment: Match individual to achievement; role-play 'what I want to be'; picture identification quiz

B1.3.1.1.1.cs_desc: Show understanding of Europeans who came to Ghana.

B1.3.1.1.1.competencies: Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship; Digital Literacy; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
B1.3.1.1.1.resources: World map; European country flag cards – Portugal, Britain, France, Sweden, Germany/Brandenburg, Denmark, Netherlands, Norway; timeline strips; museum pictures

B1.3.1.1.1.assessment: Ordering Europeans by arrival; map location task; oral Q&A
